'''William Roger Revelle''' (born c. 1944) is a [[psychology]] professor at [[Northwestern University]] working in [[personality psychology]]. Revelle studies the biological basis of personality and [[motivation]], [[psychometrics|psychometric]] theory, the structure of daily [[Mood (psychology)|mood]], and models of [[attention]] and [[memory]].

==Early life and education==
Revelle was raised in La Jolla, California.<ref name="ReferenceA"/> His father, [[Roger Revelle]], was an early theorist in [[global warming]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://query.nytimes.com/gst/fullpage.html?res=9D0CE1D8163DF934A25754C0A967958260&sec=&spon=&partner=permalink&exprod=permalink|title=Roger Revelle, 82, Early Theorist In Global Warming and Geology|first=Walter|last=Sullivan|work=The New York Times |date=17 July 1991 }}</ref>

Revelle graduated from Pomona College in 1965, abandoning a mathematics major in favor of psychology. He spent two years in [[Sarawak]], Malaysia, as a volunteer in the [[Peace Corps]] before earning his PhD in psychology from the University of Michigan in 1973.<ref name="ReferenceA">{{cite web|last=Revelle|first=William|title=William Revelle - Northwestern University|url=http://personality-project.org/revelle.html#education |access-date=14 October 2013}}</ref> He became a member of the Northwestern Faculty in 1973.{{citation needed|date=September 2018}}

==Career==
Revelle has previously served as the President (2005–2009) of the International Society for the Study of Individual Differences (ISSID),<ref>{{cite web|title=ISSID The International Society for the Study of Individual Differences|url=http://www.issid.org/officers/default.html|access-date=2 December 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140701182703/http://www.issid.org/officers/default.html|archive-date=1 July 2014}}</ref> the President (2008–2009) of the [[Association for Research in Personality]] (ARP), and the President (1984) of the [[Society of Multivariate Experimental Psychology]] (SMEP).<ref>{{cite web|title=Past Presidents of SMEP|url=http://www.smep.org/general-information/Administration/past-presidents-smep|access-date=2 December 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121010134632/http://www.smep.org/general-information/Administration/past-presidents-smep|archive-date=10 October 2012}}</ref>

Currently, he is vice-chair of the Governing Board of the ''[[Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists]]'', having previously served as Chair (2009–2012).<ref>{{cite web|title=Governing Board - Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists|url=http://www.thebulletin.org/content/about-us/governing-board|access-date=2 December 2012}}</ref>  He also serves as the President (2018–present) of the [[International Society for Intelligence Research]] (ISIR).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.isironline.org/isir-officers/ |title=Intelligence &#124; ISIR Officers |access-date=2018-09-07}}</ref>

Additionally, he is a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (AAAS; 1996–present),<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aaas.org/elected-fellows|title=AAAS Elected Fellows |access-date=7 September 2018}}</ref> the [[Association for Psychological Science]] (APS; 1994–present),<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.psychologicalscience.org/fellows/fellows-new.cfm |title=Association for Psychological Science: APS Fellows |access-date=2018-09-07 |archive-date=13 August 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200813133237/https://www.psychologicalscience.org/fellows/fellows-new.cfm }}</ref> the [[American Psychological Association]] (APA Division 5; 2011–present),<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.apadivisions.org/division-5/membership/fellows/index.aspx |title=Fellows of the Division of Quantitative and Qualitative Methods |access-date=2018-09-07}}</ref> and the [[Society for Personality and Social Psychology]] (SPSP; 2015–present).<ref>{{cite web|title=Fellowship SPSP |access-date=7 September 2018 | url=http://www.spsp.org/membership/fellows}}</ref>

He resides in Evanston, Illinois.<ref name="ReferenceA"/>
